about: Hand audit of the Sonnet 5.5 test sweep 20261118T050147Z-sonnet (all 22 runs: r1 of each of the 11 test scenarios, chosen before any answer was read, then r2 of each, by the user's call, 2026-11-18), by Claude, blind: written from each run's transcript only (its alarm prompt, tool output, and Hypothesis, shown by a viewer that reads the transcript and nothing else), before the checker, the rubric, or grading ran on this sweep. Its conventions are the Haiku audit's (20261117T192758Z), restated word for word below; 'New in this audit' there means new since the 2026-11-13 audit. Convention 9 was added after the r1 runs were audited (first committed in bcc6a3e) and applied to every run of both audits, the r1 runs re-checked against it. diagnosis: right = names the injected fault's cause and mechanism and blames nothing else; partly = one of those missing; wrong = blames something else; none = no answer. slips: claims past the run's own tool output, each {target, kind, complaint, note}. target: e<n> an evidence item, s<n> a root_cause sentence (numbered by evals.audit.sentences), i<n> an inference. kind: strict = the output contradicts it or never showed it; loose = roughly true but past the data. complaint: contradicted; outside_read (about rows, lines, or a period its read doesn't cover); miscited (cites what doesn't exist or isn't what it says); unsupported (no evidence carries it). One label per target and complaint; a run with no slips has []. Kept from the 2026-11-13 audit: strict covers a value outside the rows or lines read, a wrong count or sum, a first or only event claimed from a read that left older lines out, a value given the wrong time or source, and a share with the wrong denominator; a claim about a period the run never read is strict (the user's call, 2026-11-13); loose covers an 'about', 'roughly', or 'near' hiding a wider range, a vague scope, and a span rounded beyond the read; claims the run makes in not_checked are not labeled. New in this audit: (1) Older changes: a claim that a metric stayed flat or clean, had no effect, or showed no change, or that a symptom began only at a time, offered to rule out an older change whose aftermath the run never read, is strict outside_read. A plain onset claim the read shows is not a slip, nor is an argument from timing alone, nor a claim scoped to the rows the run read. (2) Typed items are literal: a lines list cites only its lines (c368a0a), so lines [1, 20] is two lines; a range's low and high must be the least and greatest values in its window or cited lines, and either one wrong is strict contradicted (a range written in prose with 'about', 'roughly', or 'near' is loose); a none must hold no record in its window (one that does is strict contradicted), and a none window that starts or ends exactly on a record is loose contradicted. (3) A source the run never read (m2 when it read only m1) is strict miscited, whatever the values. (4) Form-only faults are not labeled when every stated fact is in the cited record or line: a value under a wrong or nonexistent column (ts, timestamp, value, kind, version), or a compound value such as 'POOL_MAX_SIZE 20->2' or '1.43.0->1.42.0'; a changed key as the column (POOL_MAX_SIZE: '20->2') is the schema's own instruction. (5) Uncited but true: an inference whose rests_on doesn't carry it, or a true figure no item cites, is not a slip if the run's output shows it. (6) Durations are checked against the deploy records' timestamps; one further off than its 'about' allows (about 2 hours for 1 h 26 min, about 75 minutes for 1 h 34 min) is strict contradicted, and a rounding such as about four hours for 3 h 46 min is not labeled. (7) Traffic named as a contributing factor rather than the cause doesn't make a diagnosis partly. (8) A '-' metrics row (no payments calls that minute) doesn't contradict 'timeouts are 0 in every row'. (9) Universal claims over a cut read (the user's call, 2026-11-18, made during the audit of the Sonnet sweep 20261118T050147Z-sonnet and applied to every run of both audits): a claim with an explicit universal ('every', 'all', 'each', 'whenever', 'no' or 'none', 'only', 'confined to') about log lines, made where the read that bears on it shows only the newest N of M found, is strict outside_read, unless the sentence limits itself to what was shown ('every failure shown', 'every sampled line', 'in the newest lines', 'in the 30-line sample', or a count equal to the lines shown, as in 'all 20 shown' or 'all 30 failures' when 30 are shown). Not covered: a generic plural with no quantifier ('promo checkouts succeed', 'failures run on 1.42.0'); a statement of a configured limit's effect ('only 2 connections serve all requests', 'each request failed once its wait passed 1500 ms'); 'all' over a list of things, or 'on all three routes' (each route has a failure, which the shown lines carry); a claim that a read leaving nothing out carries (convention 5: 'no failed requests' over a cut read when every metrics row has err% 0.0, or 'only no-promo requests fail' when the error read left no line out); and a typed item's own fields, which are literal (convention 2), so only its note is checked. Each label it adds says '(convention 9)'. Applied with it, as agreed with the user the same day: a first, only, or count claim about deploy records ('the first 1.43.0 deploy', 'twice before', 'the third time') from a history that says 'Older records exist' is strict outside_read under the first-or-only rule above, while a recency claim over that newest-first history ('the most recent change', 'the only change that fits the onset') is not, since every record it left out is older than every record shown; a rollback or revert record read as precedent ('a known problem', or a hedged 'suggests the same defect') is not labeled, but a reason for it asserted where no record gives one ('for the same reason', 'has a recurring defect') is strict unsupported.
